parts:
Hi There! I have a survey with 5-Point Likert with 33 items and 394 respondents. I want to run a CFA model. My assumptions are that the questions follow this model:

cfa_esp <- '# Definição das Variáveis latentes (CFA)

# Para o Bloco 2 (Rede Colaborativa: RC)

coop =~ CM11 + CM21 + CM31 + CM33

funcao =~ CM4 + CM5 + CM10 + CM19 + CM32

esforço =~ CM1 + CM8 + CM14 + CM16 + CM20 + CM25 + CM28 + CM30

punicao =~ CM2 + CM7 + CM9 + CM15 + CM18 + CM27

desigual =~ CM3 + CM13 + CM17 + CM22 + CM24 + CM26 + CM29

rivalidade =~ CM6 + CM12 + CM23

'

 So, based on this question I used MLR estimator:

m0_cfa <- cfa(cfa_esp, data =data, std.lv = T, orthogonal = F, estimator = "MLR")

And it runs fine (I don’t need to use ordered=T here).

lavaan 0.6-7 ended normally after 42 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML

  Optimization method                           NLMINB

  Number of free parameters                         81

  Number of observations                           394

Model Test User Model:

                                               Standard      Robust

  Test Statistic                               1455.764    1288.443

  Degrees of freedom                                480         480

  P-value (Chi-square)                            0.000       0.000

  Scaling correction factor                                   1.130

       Yuan-Bentler correction (Mplus variant)                     

Model Test Baseline Model:

  Test statistic                              5428.820    4658.793

  Degrees of freedom                               528         528

  P-value                                        0.000       0.000

  Scaling correction factor                                  1.165

User Model versus Baseline Model:

  Comparative Fit Index (CFI)                    0.801       0.804

  Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI)                       0.781       0.785

  Robust Comparative Fit Index (CFI)                         0.810

  Robust Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI)                            0.791


In my recent research and in this post I saw  that WLSMV is also a good estimator. So, I used:

# Aproach 2

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: "Guide"/Final considerations/recomendations on CFA for ordinal response variables
parts: - Also, Is there a consensus between MLR and WLSMV estimators?

5 or more categories can typically be treated as continuous with MLR, unless there are very few responses in tail categories (e.g., as a result of asymmetric thresholds), in which case 7 categories are preferred before treating as continuous:  

http://psychmodels.ucdavis.edu/uploads/8/6/3/9/86398102/rhemtullabrosseauliardsavalei_pm.pdf

- Am I doing right?

- Are the calls in cfa() correct (sintaxe/code)?

Looks fine, except you don't need the argument orthogonal=FALSE because that is the default for cfa()
Likewise, when you declare outcomes as ordered=, the default is estimator = "WLSMV", so no need for that.  
But it doesn't hurt to explicitly state either argument.

- In fitmeasures(m0_cfa), which is the print above, all what I need to look at are on the right-most measures (under “Robust” column), when there are two columns. One curious thing is that the “robust” estimators of #Aproach 2 are available under the name of “scaled”, not “robust” when I call summary(m0_cfa, fit.measures = T)

the ones explicitly labeled "robust" are consistent estimators of their population counterparts, so they are preferred to the "scaled" versions, which simply apply the normal-theory formulas to robust chi-squared statistics.

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2018.1455142
- So, how should I report the CFI indicator? (as "scaled" or "robust"?).

When "robust" is available (with MLR), report it and cite the papers that proposed them:

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2012.715252

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2014.933697

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: "Guide"/Final considerations/recomendations on CFA for ordinal response variables
parts:
If those variables are treated as ordinal, then their latent-response's residual variances are not estimable (at least, not without constraints on the thresholds).  By default (parameterization="delta"), the latent-response scales (~*~) are fixed to 1, and residual variances are merely implied as 1 minus the explained variance.

But if this is happening when you treat those variables as continuous, then something else is going on.  In which case a minimal script (and maybe some data) would be required to see what is happening.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
